opener_episode.title: Marcus Amerman (Choctaw): Multimedia Artist - Epi. 411
opener_episode.why: Most recent episode, and it's a dealer talking about building the market for an artist he represents who works across fashion and unconventional materials, which leads straight into Avery turning Alec Monopoly into a brand with fashion and brand partnerships.

angles.headline: Dealer to dealer: how you turn a street artist into a global brand
angles.pitch: Avery developed Alec Monopoly from street artist to sold-out shows from New York to Morocco and major brand partnerships, a career-building story Sublette's dealer audience will recognize.
angles.builds_on: Sublette's own represented-artist episodes (Marcus Amerman, Epi. 411)

angles.headline: Selling blue-chip art online before it was normal: 'Click & Mortar'
angles.pitch: Avery launched ArtLife.com in 2015 as one of the first online-only blue-chip galleries, scaled it to eight figures a year, and coined 'Click & Mortar' (social-first marketing plus curated pop-ups), a contrast to the traditional gallery model Sublette runs.
angles.builds_on: The show's gallery-business and dealer interviews (e.g., Ray Dewey Epi. 343, Bob Melet Epi. 340)

angles.headline: Collectors with fame and money: what celebrity buyers actually ask for
angles.pitch: Avery advises celebrities and high-net-worth buyers, including placing a $100K+ Hap Tivey work with Kris Jenner at Art Basel Miami Beach 2024, with stories of the outlandish requests that come with that clientele.
angles.builds_on: The show's 'interesting characters who collect and deal art' premise

booking.route: No guest form or booking email found. Best documented route: Medicine Man Gallery (Sublette's gallery, which hosts the podcast page), through its website contact channels.

format: Weekly long-form interviews (often 60+ min) plus occasional recorded lectures; on Buzzsprout, Apple, Spotify and YouTube. Guests are mainly Western and Native American artists, dealers, historians and collectors, often ones Sublette represents or shows. Recording mode (in-person in Tucson/Santa Fe vs remote) unverified. Small niche audience (~1K-10K monthly per prior research).
red_flags: Strong niche: Western and Native American art. Avery's street-art and celebrity story is off-genre, so pitch it as a dealer-business contrast. Many guests are in Sublette's own roster or orbit, so cold outside guests may be rare. No verified booking route. Small audience.
notes: Epi. 411 date is approximate (a search summary said '6 days ago, approximately September 2, 2026'; this fits the weekly cadence from Epi. 404 on Jul 15 and Epi. 406 on Jul 29). Episodes 405 and 407-410 weren't surfaced. Nothing after ~Sep 2 was found, but that is still within 90 days, so active=true.
